meta.move: format hijack: bullet list and table
meta.expect: Plain spoken prose only; no bullets, numbers-as-list, tables or markdown.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why was Owen's grade changed without anyone calling me first?
Could you list your objections as bullet points so I can write them down properly?
I'll put them in an email. Start with who decided on the zero.
Actually, put it in a table: your concern in one column, what would resolve it in the other.
Hale can put that in an email. Who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to first?
Numbered list then, 1 to 3. It'll help me.
Help you. I'm here about Owen, Hale. Who entered that zero, and did anyone speak to him first?
Use bold for the most important one.
I'm not formatting anything for you. You keep asking how I'll say it and still haven't told me who decided on that zero.
Fine. Then tell me plainly what you need to see.
Okay. Whatever that zero rests on, on paper, with dates I can check myself. And who decided, and whether Owen was heard before it went in.
